My XP machine is running really slow, it takes 20 minutes to boot up, and it has 220GB free, which is over 50% of the disk free. So I want to change over to a new OS that supports Windows programs and some DOS games.

Requirements:

  • Are there any OS which will run older DOS games like Call of Duty 1, Half Life 1, Command and Conquer, Warzone 2100?
  • Is this OS fairly well supported with updates and a strong user base?
  • I'd prefer to avoid linux.
  • I'd like to browse the internet also.
  • It should be a mature OS that works.

Thanks.
Are there alternatives to Windows which will run older DOS games?

If your XP machine takes 20 mins to boot, you got problems. Might be infested with junk ware... A clean copy of XP on semi good hardware can boot in less than a minute.

Might want to think about a clean install.
I don't have the original XP CD, only the valid product key, and I can't find a reliable source for an XP install ISO or CD. It's a Gateway machine, it never came with an XP CD.

You can probably find a torrent for the ISO. Don't get a cracked version and make sure to deactivate windows before you reinstall. You should be able to then reuse the key. It's a good idea to back up and reinstall your OS every few years with windows.

I personally agree with @Poppamunz though. I suggest a GNU/Linux distro. I use Debian.

How do I make sure the Win XP torrent is not cracked though?

p.s. Malwarebytes reports no malware when I did a scan.
It should say in the torrent description. If you find something that has an additional workaround you can probably just use the image and ignore the crack.

Warzone 2100 is not a DOS game, it's been open sourced, and you can run it on modern windows, and there's even a linux port. Even though you don't want to use it, it's pretty impressive.

Red Alert 1 has also been made freely available.

Otherwise, no, what you are asking for doesn't exist. If you want a mature OS that works and can browse the internet, and isn't windows, that'd be Linux. ReactOS (an attempt to make a non-windows windows) is a thing, but it isn't mature, and doesn't successfully meet your other goals yet.

A Windows XP machine would be in the neighborhood of 9 years old or older at this point. There are definitely XP machines still in circulation, still chugging away, but they aren't designed to last forever. at 5+ years you really start seeing hardware failures build up. When it falls that far out of date, it's hard to keep it safe and functional online.

My recommendation would be to back up your data from this machine, and then wipe it clean. find a copy of XP with Service Pack 2, and install that, then shoot the updater in the head by going into Services.msc and stopping the windows update service, then disabling it. Don't use it for browsing, don't use it for anything important, just use it for your old games that you can't run in modern windows. Don't bother with an antivirus, but keep it behind a firewall, or even leave it off the network entirely. Security wise, it's going to be a nightmare regardless of what patch level you're at, so it's only really going to do you good as a game console.

I'd also look for somebody who does computer work, and see if they can help you max out the ram for your system. the amount of RAM you have is going to be a lot more relevant to how it performs, than how much disk space you have occupied.
